newsitem.title: USA: Mass. expands open competition in power market.
newsitem.headline: Mass. expands open competition in power market.

text.p: Boston Edison Co and Eastern Utilities Associates reached agreement Monday with Massachusetts officials on a plan that would expand open competition in the state's retail electricity market, the state's attorney general said in a statement.

The two utilities join a pact signed earlier with Massachusetts Electric Co to implement a plan by Attorney General Scott Harshbarger and state Energy Commissioner David O'Connor to offer consumers a choice of electricity supplier.

With the addition of the two, about 67 percent of the state's residential and business consumers currently buying power from investor-owned utilities will be able to choose their power supplier from January 1, 1998, the statement said.
- A "Standard Offer" fixed rate cut of at least 10 percent for business and residential customers on their monthly power bills;
- A provision that allows consumers a one-time option to leave the competitive market and return to the 10 percent Standard Offer rate cut'
- The divestiture of all non-nuclear generating plants "in a way that could lower consumer bills more than 10 percent, while allowing the utilities to recover so-called stranded costs";
- And protections for low-income consumers, utility employees affected by the transition to a competitive market, and communities with power plants.
